title: The Zero Paradox: A Multi-Framework Mathematical Ontology
description: A formal mathematical framework, verified sorry-free in Lean 4 + Mathlib across lattice algebra, p-adic topology, information theory, functional analysis, and category theory, whose central theorem T-SNAP proves the shape of the Binary Snap, the step from the bottom element ⊥ of a two-state carrier to the state above it (named ε₀ in that chart), and not that the step occurs: occurrence rests on the framework's occurrence commitment (with DA-1), not on T-SNAP (what T-SNAP is and is not: ZeroParadox/Order/SnapCannotBe.lean, Sections I-II). The step's join is derived from the bottom-element axiom of join-semilattice theory, with no snap-specific axiom, and that a first step above ⊥ exists at all rests on the framework's one substantive modelling commitment, discrete states (AX-B1); T-SNAP depends on no Lean axioms (#print axioms is empty); Classical.choice appears in the realization layers, mostly inherited from Mathlib but not only there, and in two places the general statement proved with choice implies excluded middle or its weak form, by a choice-free reduction (ZeroParadox/AxiomProfile.lean). The formal layers included, each verified sorry-free in Lean 4 + Mathlib, are: ZP-A (lattice algebra), ZP-B (p-adic topology), ZP-C (information theory), ZP-D (functional analysis / state layer), ZP-E (cross-framework synthesis / T-SNAP derivation), ZP-F (counterexamples - the snap fails in all ordered fields), ZP-G (category theory), ZP-H (categorical bridge, with the snap floor realized as genuine functors into the real Mathlib categories TopCat, ModuleCat ℂ, and the Kleisli category of the probability monad), ZP-I (inside zero), ZP-J (self-reference / AFA decoration uniqueness / wheel of fractions - division by zero as a total operation), ZP-K (computational grounding), ZP-L (incomputability convergence / ε₀ as ordinal snap threshold), ZP-M (Kleene-ordinal bridge), ZP-N (the constructive snap - the ε₀ snap rebuilt syntactically from below on ordinal notations, choice-free; ZP-L's ε₀ results, as stated, carry Classical.choice in their statements; the ascent below ε₀ is restated choice-free on ordinal notations, and for ε₀ itself a choice-free Lean restatement of the fixed-point equation and its uniqueness on E0Note sets existence by definition, while a choice-free derivation in Lean of the fixed point on a well-founded carrier, leastness included, was not located as of 2026-10-08, searched as recorded in ZeroParadox/Ordinal/SnapNucleus.md), ZP-P (the fixed-point fork - a synthesis layer: least versus greatest fixed point, i.e. induction / well-founded versus coinduction / non-well-founded closure, with a choice-free Knaster–Tarski fork schema and the diagonal fixed point ⊥ at the collapse seam, where choice enters only the non-well-founded realizations and is inherited from Mathlib), and ZP-Q (the frame-change - the bottom read as both 0 and ∞: the order-theoretic frame-flip universal holds, valuation and categorical per-domain instances are built, and the categorical Lawvere universal meets a proven Cantor wall, with the cross-domain identity a type boundary), and ZP-R (cross-category fixed point - a synthesis / placement layer: the framework's self-application fixed point is a role filled per face, and ZP-R asks where that role is filled by a Lawvere fixed point across three faces: refuted in Set on every carrier except a one-element one (Cantor), free of a monotone obstruction on complete lattices (Knaster–Tarski), with no reflexive object built here and no map from the two-element chain onto its monotone self-maps (the first finite stage of Soto-Andrade and Varela's two-element example, 1984, §2.5, pp. 15–16; the case Y = 2 of Trimble's Cantor theorem for posets; Bergman 2008, Cor. 7), and realized in the computability face (Rogers / Kleene; that this fixed point is a Lawvere instance is cited); Lawvere's theorem is the translation key between the faces formalized here, not a mechanism every face instantiates, and ZP-R conjectures nothing global; its Diagonal Family Addendum maps the faces formalized here by the μ/ν fork - wall faces (Cantor, Russell, Turing, Tarski, Curry) where self-reference cannot close, and floor faces (the Quine atom, the Kleene quine, Löb / Gödel 2nd, Rice) where it does, each fixed point supplied per face - with the unification credited to Lawvere (1969) and Yanofsky (2003) and the contribution the formalization (the engine, the wall faces, and the Quine-atom and Löb / Gödel 2nd floor faces choice-free; the computability floor faces choice-carrying) and its tie to the self-application role). The framework's claims are mapped against established prior art in a 'Convergence with established work' ledger (CLAIMS.md), with credit pointing outward and an honest delta for each, and the claim graph itself is machine-checked (ZeroParadox/ClaimsMirror.lean), each proved status a verified link to a green Lean declaration rather than a label; and a ZP-J Keystone Addendum records two machine-checked investigations of the keystone (the self-referential 'diagonal' fixed point at the floor): a face-by-face Lawvere verdict, and the binary snap as a crossing of the well-foundedness boundary (Taylor; Adámek-Milius-Moss), with the full coalgebraic version flagged open.
